syntheses.title: Lack of unified evaluation metrics and scenario diversity across driving policy studies
syntheses.body: The claims reveal a gap in the evaluation of driving policies due to differences in scenario design and evaluation metrics. Paper B uses specific scenarios such as 'Nudging around a parked car' with defined locations and speeds (claim e66cdad4-7032-5789-a29f-c11a77e8e472) and observes agent behavior for stopping, collision, or passing (claim 54114bd0-b0d6-5887-9da8-ce02a07fa15b). Paper A emphasizes the importance of provided signals for training and evaluation (claim 45e57524-d848-53c8-a93c-617d8480da8e8) and studies multiple autonomous driving approaches (claim 34863bb0-827c-5405-a15d-f7229ca8985c). Paper C provides datasets with diverse roads, lighting, and weather conditions (claims 5b04c50f-7b96-5ddd-a0be-8eb2d45b4a96 and a233e152-9b2f-5df6-a121-2115da13cae8) but does not specify scenario-based evaluation metrics. This indicates a gap in standardized, comprehensive evaluation scenarios and metrics across these studies, limiting direct comparison and generalization of driving policy performance.
